4th Period.workingNow: Researching one assigned AI topic — bias, misinformation, privacy, overreliance, environmental cost, or accessibility — from teacher-provided sources only, no AI chat.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A persuasive 'How I Think We Should Use AI' article live on your portfolio site — your argued position on the best way to use AI, backed by this week's research, plus at least one image — pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can research at least two pieces of evidence about my assigned AI topic from real sources so that I have material to support my own opinion tomorrow.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.IC.21 — Discuss issues of bias and accessibility in the design of existing technologies.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining orally how an author uses language to support ideas.
agenda: Warm-Up: recall yesterday's never-share rules (3 min)
Quick overview + research packet handout (3 min)
I do: model reading a source, claim + evidence (8 min)
We do: annotate one shared source together (8 min)
You do: research team digs into your topic (20 min)
Team share-out: 30 seconds per topic (6 min)
Exit Ticket: one fact for tomorrow's article (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you learned to protect your own data. Today, in research teams, you dig into the bigger risks and benefits of AI as a technology. Tomorrow you take everything the class found and turn it into your own persuasive argument.

6th Period.workingNow: Predicting 2 dynamics — things that will happen during play — that your mechanics will create.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: MDA framework notes (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) + a one-page Game Design Plan for your SchoolAI game, shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can predict a dynamic that will emerge from my mechanics so that I can design toward the feeling I actually want.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining orally how an author uses language to support ideas.
agenda: I do: how mechanics create dynamics, modeled (12 min)
We do: trace one dynamic from a shared game (10 min)
You do: predict 2 dynamics your mechanics will create (18 min)
Exit Ticket: one dynamic + why it happens (5 min)
6th Period.connections: You've named your mechanics and your aesthetic — the rules and the feeling. Dynamics is the bridge between them: what actually happens when someone plays. This is the hardest piece, and tomorrow you put all three together into your design plan.
